title: Taurine modulates IKr but not IKs in guinea‐pig ventricular cardiomyocytes

sections.abstract: <jats:p> <jats:list list-type="explicit-label"> <jats:list-item><jats:p>Effects of taurine on the delayed rectifier K<jats:sup>+</jats:sup> current (I<jats:sub>K</jats:sub>) in isolated guinea‐pig ventricular cardiomyocytes were examined at different intracellular Ca<jats:sup>2+</jats:sup> concentration ([Ca<jats:sup>2+</jats:sup>]<jats:sub>i</jats:sub>), using whole‐cell voltage and current clamp techniques. Experiments were performed at 36°C.</jats:p></jats:list-item> <jats:list-item><jats:p>Addition of taurine (10–20 m<jats:sc>M</jats:sc>) decreased the action potential duration (APD) at pCa 8, but increased the APD at pCa 6. Taurine (20 m<jats:sc>M</jats:sc>) enhanced I<jats:sub>K</jats:sub> at 70 mV by 22.4±3.1% (<jats:italic>n</jats:italic>=6, <jats:italic>P</jats:italic><0.01) at pCa 8, whereas taurine inhibited the I<jats:sub>K</jats:sub> by 27.1±2.7% (<jats:italic>n</jats:italic>=6, <jats:italic>P</jats:italic><0.01) at pCa 6. These responses behaved in a concentration‐dependent manner.</jats:p></jats:list-item> <jats:list-item><jats:p>The I<jats:sub>K</jats:sub> is composed of the rapid and slow components (I<jats:sub>Kr</jats:sub> and I<jats:sub>Ks</jats:sub>). When [Ca<jats:sup>2+</jats:sup>]<jats:sub>i</jats:sub> was pCa 6, taurine at 20 m<jats:sc>M</jats:sc> reduced the tail current of I<jats:sub>Kr</jats:sub> at 70 mV by 16.5±2.7% (<jats:italic>n</jats:italic>=5, <jats:italic>P</jats:italic><0.05) and that of I<jats:sub>Ks</jats:sub> at 70 mV by 27.1±2.8% (<jats:italic>n</jats:italic>=6, <jats:italic>P</jats:italic><0.01). In contrast, at pCa 8, the tail currents of I<jats:sub>Kr</jats:sub> and I<jats:sub>Ks</jats:sub> at 70 mV were enhanced by 13.4±3.2% (<jats:italic>n</jats:italic>=7, <jats:italic>P</jats:italic><0.05) and by 22.4±3.1% (<jats:italic>n</jats:italic>=7, <jats:italic>P</jats:italic><0.01), respectively. The voltages of half‐maximum activation (V<jats:sub>1/2</jats:sub>) for I<jats:sub>Kr</jats:sub> and I<jats:sub>Ks</jats:sub> were not modified by taurine.</jats:p></jats:list-item> <jats:list-item><jats:p>Addition of E‐4031 (5 μ<jats:sc>M</jats:sc>) to taurine had a complete blockade of the tail current of I<jats:sub>Kr</jats:sub>, but not I<jats:sub>Ks</jats:sub>. The remained tail current (I<jats:sub>Ks</jats:sub>) in the presence of E‐4031 (5 μ<jats:sc>M</jats:sc>) was not affected by taurine (20 m<jats:sc>M</jats:sc>), but was blocked by 293B (30 μ<jats:sc>M</jats:sc>).</jats:p></jats:list-item> <jats:list-item><jats:p>These results indicate that taurine modulates I<jats:sub>Kr</jats:sub> but not I<jats:sub>Ks</jats:sub>, depending on [Ca<jats:sup>2+</jats:sup>]<jats:sub>i</jats:sub>, resulting in regulation of the APD.</jats:p></jats:list-item> </jats:list> </jats:p><jats:p><jats:italic>British Journal of Pharmacology</jats:italic> (1999) <jats:bold>126</jats:bold>, 87–92; doi:<jats:ext-link xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" ext-link-type="doi" xlink:href="10.1038/sj.bjp.0702308">10.1038/sj.bjp.0702308</jats:ext-link></jats:p>
